why: The new fallback ordering rule kept verbs/auxiliaries with their complements, shifting preferred cuts away from verb-complement splits; that helped deeper/long-budget positions slightly (≤99) but reduced agreement at the top ranks and hurt short-latency bins (≤3, ≤5, ≤7) by forcing cuts into noun compounds and internal phrase boundaries instead of the earlier verb splits.
lesson: Do not let a fallback that protects verb–complement adjacency override constraints that prevent splitting tight noun compounds or internal phrase material, because that tradeoff improves long-budget rank depth at the cost of short-latency quality.
